78778.subject: Tokenized Stocks Traded $1 Billion With The Market Shut

These are the biggest stories in DeFi and crypto:

* **[Tokenized stocks](https://thedefiant.io/news/tradfi-and-fintech/tokenized-stocks-traded-1-billion-while-the-stock-market-was-shut)**[ traded $1 billion while U.S. exchanges were shut](https://thedefiant.io/news/tradfi-and-fintech/tokenized-stocks-traded-1-billion-while-the-stock-market-was-shut)

* **[The Ethereum Foundation](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/ethereum-foundation-sets-2029-quantum-target-and-narrows-hegot-scope)**[ set a December 2029 quantum-resistance deadline](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/ethereum-foundation-sets-2029-quantum-target-and-narrows-hegot-scope)

* **[Oasis Vault](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/oasis-vault-cryptopunk-909-giveaway-self-custody?utm_source=newsletter&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=tokenized-stocks-traded-1-billion-with-the-market-shut)**[ is giving away CryptoPunk 909 (Partner)](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/oasis-vault-cryptopunk-909-giveaway-self-custody?utm_source=newsletter&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=tokenized-stocks-traded-1-billion-with-the-market-shut)

The New York Stock Exchange was closed for 89 and a half hours. Tokenized versions of its listings traded $1.41 billion.

Saturday brought $490.3 million and Sunday $516.9 million across the 42 largest tokenized equities, and [the weekend's $1.01 billion nearly matched the $1.02 billion those same tokens did on Friday with the cash market open all session](https://thedefiant.io/news/tradfi-and-fintech/tokenized-stocks-traded-1-billion-while-the-stock-market-was-shut). Labor Day added $398.3 million. Robinhood's tokens took $572.8 million of the weekend, 57% of the measured total, ahead of Binance's bStocks at $303.5 million.

Robinhood leads on turnover while holding the smallest book: $133.2 million of tokenized equities against Ondo's $860 million and xStocks' $631.2 million. Caption: 

# Matryoshka money laundering

Lucy Edwards, a relationship manager at the Bank of New York, opened an account in 1995 for Benex International Co., a defunct company with an empty office in Queens, NY.

Benex was owned by her husband, Peter Berlin, who allowed one of Edwards’ customers, Russia’s Depozitarno-Kliringovy Bank (DKB), to use the company’s account to move money in and out of the Bank of New York (BoNY).

DKB was provided with Bank of New York software that allowed customers to independently wire money out of their accounts. Over the subsequent four years, the Russian bank used the software to move an estimated $7 billion in and out of the Bank of New York on behalf of its own customers.

Regulators recognized this for what it was: correspondent banking.

“I agreed to actively assist DKB to operate what was, in effect, a banking business in the United States,” Berlin [later](https://bbb.livejournal.com/1780691.html) confessed, “even though none of these entities had a license from the US government to operate as a bank or to operate a branch or agency in the United States.”

“Correspondent banking” is banking for banks: when a US bank opens an account that lets a non-US bank move dollars on behalf of its customers, for example. (Because US dollars can only move between US banks.)

It's the arrangement that lets the rest of the world do business in dollars, which is good: It allows US dollars to facilitate global trade, to everyone’s advantage — and the US’ advantage most of all. 

Sometimes it is bad.

DKB used the Benex account to help customers evade Russia’s capital controls by switching their rubles into dollars and moving them offshore. 

In other words, Benex was using its BoNY account to act as a correspondent bank.

Sometimes it was used for legitimate Russian businesses fearing the chaotic Russian government would appropriate its assets. Other times it was mobsters, oligarchs, and corrupt politicians.

It did this illegally. The Bank of New York did not know that’s how its account was being used.

Caption: 

Welcome to the DefiLlama Newsletter. Each week we bring you the most valuable onchain insights from the the deepest DeFi dataset in the world.



# Onchain Insights: Charts this Week

### Robinhood Chain vs Base: head to head

Robinhood Chain is two months into mainnet. Base is three years in.

Compare Chains (https://defillama.com/compare-chains?chains=Base&chains=Robinhood+Chain&tvlChart=true&dexVolumeChart=true&chainFeesChart=true&chainRevenueChart=true)

Base’s larger and more mature TVL base has more distributed DEX volume in a DeFi-focused ecosystem. Robinhood Chain’s tokenized equity focus and strong distribution are pushing non-stablecoin RWA market cap above Base’s.

Despite only carrying one-sixth of Base’s TVL, Robinhood Chain’s DEX volume, app revenue and chain fees are outpacing Base.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/f37fda48-4906-44df-9c67-badc754bf7d3/daily-app-revenue-robinhood-chain-vs-base_2026-09-08.png?t=1788890836)
Caption: 

Robinhood Chain has facilitated more volume than Base over the last 30d and 3x Base’s volume in the last week, growing on 7d, 14d and 30d timeframes. DEX volume on Base is up 23% over 30d but fell 6% over the last 7d.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/246921f6-5df2-47e8-941c-23ae85404d37/daily-dex-volume-robinhood-chain-vs-base_2026-09-08.png?t=1788883801)
Caption: 

The protocols facilitating the volume and bringing in revenue for both chains look different: on Base, Aerodrome and Uniswap facilitate the most DEX volume and bring in the most revenue.

On Robinhood Chain, Uniswap facilitates over 70% of DEX volume, but ranks third among Robinhood Chain’s revenue generators. GMGN and Pons earned 2x and 3x more than Uniswap over the last month.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/cd1e92a8-9f74-45e6-8bcd-d2cdef92d7aa/robinhood-chain-top-8-protocols-by-dex-volume-30d_2026-09-08.png?t=1788883810)

*Metaplanet* shares fell nearly 10% in Japan on Tuesday, extending a two-session slide of about 17% after a public note from CEO *Simon Gerovich* failed to calm investors.

* The issue relates to the firm's Series 10 option pool, which grew from about 46 million shares to 319 million because it was adjusted to remain equal to 20% of fully diluted shares rather than a fixed number.
* The structure allowed the executive award pool to grow while existing shareholders were diluted as Metaplanet continued to issue stock to buy *bitcoin*.
* Gerovich admitted Metaplanet "had not done a good enough job" communicating the company's plans and structure with shareholders, noting it froze the pool in August and added a five-year lock-up.
